result.question:
The last maintenance job on Transformer 1 at site MAIN was supposed to deal with the gassing, and I want to know whether it actually worked.

Find the most recently closed work order on Transformer 1. Give me its number, description, completion date, resolution notes and failure code, and tell me which fault it was meant to fix.

Then look at the oil samples taken after that date, within 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 to 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000. Use hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene and co. Screen hydrogen, acetylene and co for anomalous samples with a proper anomaly detection model rather than a fixed threshold. Separately, run a dissolved gas fault classification on the latest complete sample and compare its fault class with the fault the job was meant to fix.

Decide as follows:
- If both checks point to trouble, meaning at least one anomaly is flagged and the classification still shows the same fault or a higher-energy one, call the fix ineffective. Create a priority 2 corrective follow-up work order that references the original work order number, and code it with the closest failure code from our catalog.
- If only one of the two checks points to trouble, don't create a corrective job. Recommend a confirmatory oil resample within 7 days and say which check disagreed.
- If neither points to trouble, say the fix appears to have held.

If the closed job was oil filtration, degassing or regeneration, the gas levels will have been reset. In that case, judge the result on the rate of change after the job, not on absolute levels, and say you did so.

If no work order on Transformer 1 was closed before or during the window, say so, use all samples in the window, and give only the classification and anomaly result without a verdict on any fix. If fewer than 4 samples fall after the completion date, skip the anomaly model and compare the first and last post-job values instead.
result.answer:
No further tool calls are needed — I've exhausted the available avenues, so here is the result.

## Work order check
**No work order on Transformer 1 (site MAIN) has been closed** before or during 2024‑01‑15 → 2024‑01‑19 — or ever. The only WO on the asset is **1000051** (“OLTC inspection – on‑load tap changer, suspected contact wear/coking”), status **APPR**, priority 1, reported 2026‑09‑30, no completion date, no failure code. Nothing in the system attempted to deal with the gassing, so there is no fix to judge and **no verdict is given**. As instructed, I used all 4 samples in the window.

## Oil samples (2024‑01‑15 → 2024‑01‑18, ppm)
| Date | H2 | CH4 | C2H6 | C2H4 | C2H2 | CO |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 01‑15 | 2845 | 7406 | 5467 | 16684 | 7 | 32 |
| 01‑16 | 2950 | 7200 | 5400 | 16500 | 6 | 30 |
| 01‑17 | 2800 | 7300 | 5500 | 16700 | 8 | 35 |
| 01‑18 | 2900 | 7350 | 5450 | 16600 | 7 | 33 |

## Dissolved‑gas fault classification (latest complete sample, 2024‑01‑18)
The `interpret_dga` service returned “LLM unavailable” on two attempts, so I applied IEC 60599 Rogers ratios manually:
- C2H2/C2H4 = 7/16600 = **0.0004** → code 0
- CH4/H2 = 7350/2900 = **2.53** → code 2
- C2H4/C2H6 = 16600/5450 = **3.05** → code 2
- IEC code **0‑2‑2 → T3: thermal fault > 700 °C** (Duval Triangle 1 agrees: ~69 % C2H4, ~31 % CH4, <0.1 % C2H2 → T3). Confidence high — ratios sit well inside the T3 zone. Absolute levels (H2 2900, TDCG ≈ 32,400 ppm) are IEEE C57.104 Condition 4.
- Compared with the open WO 1000051: an OLTC contact‑coking hypothesis is consistent with a high‑temperature thermal fault, but that job has not been executed, so there is no before/after comparison to make.

## Anomaly screen (hydrogen, acetylene, CO)
**The model‑based screen could not be executed.** The TSFM detector path (`run_recipe`, SubLOF) requires a file pointer, no materialisation tool is available in this session, the model catalog contains no anomaly‑detection card, and probing for previously materialised files and inline `data:` URIs all failed. Rather than pass off a fixed threshold as a model result, I report the fallback you specified for small samples — first vs. last value:
- H2: 2845 → 2900 (+55 ppm, +1.9 %); range across the window 2800–2950 (±2.6 %)
- C2H2: 7 → 7 (flat; range 6–8)
- CO: 32 → 33 (+3 %; range 30–35)

Within the window no sample deviates materially from its neighbours; the gases are **stable at a very high plateau**, not spiking. (Earlier SubLOF runs logged on this asset today with the same 4‑sample window flagged at most one point — 2024‑01‑16 — in one channel and none in the rest; I could not verify which channel, so I do not rely on that.)

**Bottom line:** no closed job to evaluate; classification = **T3 high‑temperature thermal fault**; anomaly screen = **not executable by model, no step‑change in H2/C2H2/CO across the window**. No corrective or resample WO was created. If you can materialise the series to a CSV (e.g. under `/tmp/tsfm_work/`), I can run the SubLOF screen immediately.
